readout_other: Two-bottle choice ethanol and water intake; blood alcohol concentration (Analox AM1)
direction_notes: No neural readout. Treated mice reduced ethanol intake (about 51% mean reduction) and increased water intake versus sham, which increased ethanol intake.
safety_notes: Thermal safety evaluation of repeated LIFU listed as future work; no adverse events described.

exposures.label: USg-LIFU of the VTA in cHAP mice

timing.protocol_description: Pulsed sonication with pulse duration 0.5 ms and PRF 1 kHz (50% duty cycle), 15 s per session, six sessions on alternating days (days 15 to 25), delivered after UT-FEM guided mechanical alignment under isoflurane.

source_quotes.n_subjects: In-vivo neuromodulatory effects were tested in cHAP mice (n = 10) that underwent six USg-LIFU sessions targeting the VTA on alternating days and compared with sham controls (n = 5).
source_quotes.n_sessions_per_subject: Following baseline assessment, mice entered the intervention phase, spanned Days 15 through 25, during which six image-guided LIFU therapy sessions were delivered on alternate days.
source_quotes.exposures[0].fundamental_frequency_khz: For in-vivo neuromodulation, the LIFU subsystem consists of a single-element focused ultrasound transducer (SEFUST) (H101; Sonic Concepts; centre frequency of 1.3 MHz; 70 mm aperture; 51 mm focal length) with a pulser-receiver and power amplifier.
source_quotes.exposures[0].timing.pulse_duration_ms: In accordance with the International Transcranial Ultrasonic Stimulation Safety and Standards (ITRUSST) reporting guidelines [34], the pulsed sonication protocol consisted of a pulse duration (PD) of 0.5 ms and a pulse repetition frequency (PRF) of 1 kHz, resulting in a duty cycle of 50%.

flags.reason: Paper calls the intensities 'estimated in-situ' (citing ref 35) without saying whether simulated, derated or measured.
Sham mice had handling, anaesthesia, positioning and coupling but no LIFU; how the no-output condition was produced is not described.
An ex vivo HIFU lesion experiment and 2D FEM simulations are also reported but give no stimulation parameters and are not recorded as exposures.
